title: Great Britain Reach Davis Cup Semi-Finals After Thrilling Doubles Decider
summary:
Great Britain is heading to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019 — and it came down to one thrilling doubles match. Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won the deciding tie against Germany in Bologna on Thursday, November 26, sealing the win.

The Davis Cup is a team tennis contest, with countries facing off in singles and doubles matches. Britain's tie against Germany went the full distance. Cameron Norrie gave Britain the lead with a three-set win over Jan-Lennard Struff. Then world number one Alexander Zverev levelled the tie by beating British number one Arthur Fery in straight sets, 6-3, 6-2.

That set up a winner-takes-all doubles decider. Patten and Skupski — playing together for the first time since announcing they will team up for the 2027 season — proved too clinical for Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz. The win carried extra meaning for Skupski: he had lost a Davis Cup quarter-final alongside Joe Salisbury against the same German pair in December 2021, and that defeat was on his mind as the match went on.

Britain now faces Spain in the semi-final on Saturday. Spain reached the last four after Daniel Merida and Rafael Jodar won their singles matches, so the team did not need to play doubles — which let Carlos Alcaraz rest. Captain David Ferrer said Alcaraz may be in contention to play singles against Britain. In Friday's other semi-final, defending champions Italy play the Czech Republic.

It is also a special moment for captain Leon Smith, who has led the team since 2010 and will step down at the end of the tournament. Britain has won the Davis Cup 10 times, most recently in 2015. Smith said he felt the same pressure, nerves and butterflies as always, and that he is thrilled for his players.
why_it_matters: Team contests like the Davis Cup show that success in sport is not only about one star player — every match counts, and a doubles pair can decide a whole tie. It also shows how players can bounce back from a painful defeat, as Skupski did.

background_read: The Davis Cup is a team tennis contest in which countries play against each other instead of individual players playing only for themselves.
A tie between two countries is made up of singles matches, where one player faces another, and a doubles match, where two players team up on each side.
The team that wins the most matches wins the tie, so when the singles matches are split, everything can come down to the final doubles match.
Britain had not reached the semi-finals since 2019, which is why this win mattered so much to the team and its captain.
